title: The canonical intersection recovers the rational module
statement: With prime ℓ, normed E/Q_ℓ and coefficients [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], let p:U→X be qcqs, P a rational module on X, M an integral module on U and e:Ext(M)≅p^*P. The canonical rationalization Ext(N)→P of N defined in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-lattice-intersection] is invertible. No local-freeness, surjectivity or finite-etale hypothesis is required for this rationalization assertion.

source.place: Section 6.8, coefficient localization and Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph; agent intersection/matrix variant

proof.text: The mate counit formula identifies extension of the pushed integral embedding followed by the rational counit with the pushforward comparison followed by p_*e. Both factors are invertible by qcqs localization and the localization counit theorem.

Exact scalar extension maps the image inclusion to a mono, and invertibility of the original pushed map after extension makes this mono epi. Mapped pullbacks then make extension of the canonical intersection inclusion invertible. Compose with the rational counit to obtain the claimed rationalization isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem continuousLatticeIntersectionRationalization_isIso
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X))
    {U : Scheme.{u}} (p : U ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) U))
    (e : (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) U)).obj M ≅
      (upperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) p).obj P) :
    IsIso (latticeIntersectionRationalization (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X P p M e)
